races.name: EBF Stallions Restricted Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
racingtv.com/freetrial Handicap

runners_data.name: Hill O Rue
runners_data.note: Kevin Ryan's hold-up performer has shown ability in good-ground company (won over 10f on soft, placed twice at this trip) and arrives 45 days fresh; best watched for a wide run to the outside as Tom Eaves tries to find daylight in what will be a congested closing stages.

runners_data.name: Naturalia
runners_data.note: Donald Whillans' five-year-old runs off a 14-day turnaround and has a striking recent record of five places from seven runs on good or good-to-soft, suggesting genuine aptitude for today's conditions; Shay Farmer's 5lb claim is material in a tight OR=62 handicap and the horse's consistent hold-up style suits the scenario of a compressed late dash.

runners_data.name: Falcon Nine
runners_data.note: Iain Jardine's six-year-old wears a hood and arrives 19 days post-run; best form at 9-10f but has placed over this trip before, and the two wins from 15 good-ground runs suggest he can go close on the surface — Billy Garritty will need to manoeuvre him early to avoid being locked in by the hold-up pack.

runners_data.name: Condotti
runners_data.note: Hugo Palmer's four-year-old is a natural hold-up horse shuffled forward on the map because the rear is overcrowded; Clifford Lee will find the true position difficult to achieve here, and the horse's poor recent form (6th, 9th, 4th on varying surfaces) tempers expectations even if a clean run materialises.

runners_data.name: Sweet Kiss
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's sole front-runner in the race, Sweet Kiss carries the race's lone genuine pace role with Jake Dickson's 7lb claim; ten runs on good ground with only two wins and two places suggest she may be vulnerable if the field closes late, but an uncontested lead is a meaningful tactical asset.

runners_data.name: Tee Aitch Aye
runners_data.note: Jardine's five-year-old sits in the rear-heavy cluster that makes up the redistributed group — a horse whose recent form (6th, 7th, 10th on good ground) offers little encouragement on this surface, and Andrew Mullen will face a congested run attempting to hold closer ground than his natural style dictates.

runners_data.name: Royal Blaze
runners_data.note: Ewan Whillans' five-year-old, only 10 days from its last run, wears a tongue-tie and a hood and has mixed form at the trip; David Nolan pilots a horse that has only one win and one place from 15 good-ground appearances, and the style displacement toward midfield rather than his preferred hold-up berth further diminishes appeal.

runners_data.name: Tap Dancer
runners_data.note: Jim Goldie's four-year-old has decent enough recent form figures but no good-ground wins from 13 attempts and is squeezed into midfield on the map rather than the hold-up spot Paul Mulrennan would ideally secure; without a clear run late, the chance evaporates quickly.

runners_data.name: Rumbustious
runners_data.note: Charlie Johnston's three-year-old is the top-rated runner on OR=65 and arrives on a 14-day turnaround with Connor Beasley, one of the more effective riders in northern handicaps; three consecutive fourths on good ground in staying trips shows consistency without the winning punch, but the form profile is solid for this class.

runners_data.name: Storm On Jura
runners_data.note: Jim Goldie's four-year-old carries a "fades in finish" flag that is a damning tactical note for a hold-up horse in a race with no breakaway pace — Lauren Young's 5lb claim partially offsets the weight burden, but the horse's record of zeros for wins and places on good ground (6 runs) and the finishing tendency leave little to recommend here.

runners_data.name: Shifter
runners_data.note: Wilf Storey's seven-year-old ran only yesterday, which is an extreme fitness flag requiring explanation; the horse has placed twice recently but has never won on good ground across 15 attempts, and Paula Muir's 3lb claim is insufficient compensation for the energy cost of consecutive-day racing.

runners_data.name: Parole Officer
runners_data.note: Ewan Whillans' three-year-old steps up from 7-8f on all prior form to 1m2f today, which is a significant trip query; Greg Fairley rides a horse that has finished 9th, 9th on good ground in its two most relevant efforts, and the combination of unproven stamina, 52 days off, and style displacement makes this a very difficult proposition.

races.paceDynamic: Sweet Kiss is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine rival to press her for the lead, she should dictate a controlled, honest gallop over this 1m2f trip on good ground at Ayr. The pace she sets is unlikely to be suicidal — a single leader in a 12-runner handicap on good turf at this trip typically produces a steady-to-moderate early tempo, meaning the race will compress in the home straight and the winning move will come between the two-furlong pole and the final furlong. The field holds significantly more hold-up horses than the race shape can accommodate at the rear — Condotti, Tee Aitch Aye, Parole Officer, Royal Blaze, Tap Dancer, Storm On Jura, and Shifter are all natural hold-up types competing for limited cover at the back, and those most likely to actually settle comfortably near the rear are Rumbustious, Naturalia, and Hill O Rue, who have genuine hold-up credentials and the form to be in contention late. This race shape — a single honest leader setting a sustainable pace — favours prominent racers who can track the front-runner and pounce in the straight, as well as the small number of genuine closers who find clean air, rather than the traffic-hampered pack of redistributed hold-up types who will be squeezed for racing room.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Sweet Kiss Leads, Closers Swamp
scenarios.trigger: If Sweet Kiss bowls along at a steady-to-moderate gallop and the hold-up pack masses behind her, the race sets up for a late surge from a well-positioned closer.
scenarios.body: Sweet Kiss will have dictated the fractions and the field will compress coming to the two-furlong marker, creating a cavalry charge from the pack; genuine closers with form in good-ground staying handicaps will benefit from the momentum shift.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Lands Blow
scenarios.trigger: If a prominent-tracking type sits just off Sweet Kiss's heels and kicks decisively at the two-furlong pole before the hold-up pack can gather.
scenarios.body: The pace being controlled by Sweet Kiss means the horse immediately behind her travels well within herself and has reserves to quicken; this scenario rewards a horse with sharp handicap form at the trip who can race prominently in a genuine 12-runner field.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Finds Gap
scenarios.trigger: If the tempo is honest enough to stretch the field and one genuine hold-up performer threads through a gap in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: The redistributed hold-up pack will largely cancel each other out fighting for position, but a horse with tactical pace and a clear run — such as Hill O Rue or Falcon Nine — could pick off a tiring leader in the shadow of the post.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front Runner Defies
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is slow enough that Sweet Kiss steals a march and the hold-up pack, caught shuffling for position, cannot reel her in.
scenarios.body: A truly compressed pace with 12 runners jockeying for ground in the straight will leave Sweet Kiss with a soft lead and the energy to sustain the effort; a go-forward ride from Jake Dickson, with Easterby's yard in reasonable form (T14: 6/89), makes this a live outsider scenario.

watchPoints.text: Sweet Kiss (J: Jake Dickson) is the only front-runner — watch whether she is allowed to stride on unchallenged from the gates or is immediately tracked by a prominent-type forcing the pace; the entire race shape hinges on how much daylight she gets in the first two furlongs.

The hold-up cluster of Condotti, Tee Aitch Aye, Royal Blaze, Tap Dancer, Parole Officer, Storm On Jura and Shifter will all be competing for similar ground at the rear — watch for significant traffic trouble and interference in the home straight as they attempt to find a run simultaneously.

Rumbustious (OR=65, Connor Beasley) is the highest-rated horse in the field — watch whether Beasley opts to track closer to the pace than the horse's mapped position suggests, as a prominent move from the best-handicapped runner would significantly alter the shape of the race.

Shifter ran just one day ago — watch the horse closely in the preliminary ring for any signs of fatigue or physical stress, as back-to-back racing in a 12-runner handicap on good ground demands significant physical reserve from a seven-year-old.

Naturalia and Hill O Rue are both genuine hold-up types with strong going profiles for today — watch their post-race trajectories to see whether the wide-draw option frees them from traffic, as their form is the most directly relevant to the anticipated late-race shape.

races.name: Watch Racing TV Free For 31 Days Handicap

runners_data.name: Keep Me Stable
runners_data.note: In excellent recent form with three wins from four at 7f on Good ground, Linda Perratt's six-year-old is a natural prominent racer suited to tracking a single front-runner and finishing strongly; the concern is the trainer's 0/4 run in the last 14 days, though the horse's own profile is hard to fault here.

runners_data.name: Born A Star
runners_data.note: Charlie Johnston's three-year-old has a true hold-up style that is squeezed toward midfield given the cluster of closers in this field, meaning it is unlikely to race in its natural patient position; best form figures are elusive (top finish a 4th), and the 31-day break adds uncertainty.

runners_data.name: Emery Down
runners_data.note: John Ryan's four-year-old has been running consistently mid-pack in similar company but without threatening the frame, and its history of operating on Soft and Standard going makes this Good surface a mild positive; its natural hold-up style is crowded back further than ideal given field shape, limiting its threat.

runners_data.name: Whiskey Kisses
runners_data.note: The form string shows a progressive filly at sprint trips — 2nd and 3rd over 5-6f — stepping up to 7f here for the first time since joining R Mike Smith, and while the going is fine, this trip is an open question; a genuine waiting-style horse pushed into a more prominent midfield slot given field composition, she is one to monitor as a pace beneficiary if connections ride her more forwardly.

runners_data.name: Ashen
runners_data.note: Jim Goldie's four-year-old is unexposed on this track and carries confidence from a win at 7f on Good, and Lauren Young's 5lb claim is a notable positive; in reality a hold-up horse by style, though the redistribution into midfield is not wildly out of character, and the 6/13 similar-going figures are encouraging.

runners_data.name: Blakefell
runners_data.note: Ivan Furtado's three-year-old is the lone confirmed front-runner, able to control the tempo from gate to wire over a 7f trip he has handled well (win and place); the STYLE_FIT flag is noted as he maps as Prominent rather than Lead, but Tom Eaves knows how to set a controlled pace and this is a significant tactical asset in a field with little pace pressure.

runners_data.name: Qazaq
runners_data.note: Iain Jardine's five-year-old was out just three days ago, which is a clear freshness concern, and his last six outings show no win and only two places; a natural hold-up horse nudged into midfield by field congestion, his best recent form has come at this trip and on Good ground but consistency is the issue.

runners_data.name: Slack Bob
runners_data.note: Ed Dunlop's three-year-old has placed or won in each of his last four starts and clearly has ability, though his best form figures come on Standard or Soft; a genuine hold-up horse racing a natural position, Clifford Lee will look to come with a late run but needs a stronger gallop than Blakefell is likely to set.

runners_data.name: Abduction
runners_data.note: Jim Goldie's eight-year-old veteran carries top weight and has shown he can still compete at this level (1W2P in similar going), but six-day turnaround and declining figures over this course and trip in recent starts are worth noting; he is a true hold-up horse racing his natural position and depends heavily on the pace collapsing late.

runners_data.name: The Gay Blade
runners_data.note: Iain Jardine's seven-year-old arrives in superb form — three wins from his last four including two at 7f Good — and Andrew Mullen has a strong recent record on him; a prominent racer ideally suited to sitting just off a lone front-runner, this race shape is tailor-made for his style and the 6-day turnaround is no concern given his record fresh.

runners_data.name: Native Honey
runners_data.note: Jim Goldie's four-year-old has a recent 7f Good win on her CV but followed it with a string of poor efforts (7th, 10th, 15th in similar company), and 10 runners from 15 on similar going have finished outside the places; her true hold-up style is in role here but she needs everything to go right late.

runners_data.name: Eve's Boy
runners_data.note: Michael Dods' four-year-old has been placed just once from six runs and the form string over 8f does not inspire confidence stepping down to 7f, with seven of 15 similar-going runs resulting in a 7th; a hold-up horse in natural position but without the recent form or tactical edge to take advantage even if the pace unfolds his way.

races.paceDynamic: Blakefell is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 12-runner 7f handicap on Good ground at Ayr, and with no genuine pace rival to pressure him, Tom Eaves can dictate a measured, controlled tempo from the off. Keep Me Stable and The Gay Blade are the likeliest prominent chasers, tracking Blakefell through the early stages and ensuring the race is run at a fair but not frantic gallop. The majority of the field — including Ashen, Abduction, Native Honey, Slack Bob and Eve's Boy — will be operating from midfield to rear, though several of these are true hold-up types redistributed from their natural position given the volume of closer-types in this field; among those, Ashen and Abduction are best placed to actually secure handy ground given their tactical versatility. A controlled single-pace scenario on Good turf over 7f strongly favours horses who can sit prominently and quicken from a good position, rather than those waiting for a gaps off a pace that may never truly collapse.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Blakefell Dictates, Front Pair Score
scenarios.trigger: If Blakefell sets a measured gallop unchallenged and the race develops at a steady-to-fair tempo throughout.
scenarios.body: Blakefell controls from the front with Tom Eaves dictating terms, and those immediately tracking him — Keep Me Stable and The Gay Blade — are ideally placed to pounce in the final furlong on a track that rewards prominent positioning; with no pace collapse, hold-up horses are left with insufficient momentum from behind.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Types Dominate Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is just competitive enough to string the field out but the leaders keep enough in reserve to repel closers.
scenarios.body: The Gay Blade and Keep Me Stable, both sitting prominently off Blakefell's steady fractions, have the energy reserves to surge clear in the final 2f as the true hold-up horses fail to generate the momentum needed on a sound surface; this scenario rewards tactical riders who track the pace rather than come from off it.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough that the front pair empty and a well-placed closer finds a seam in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Abduction or Native Honey, racing from midfield with proven ability at this track and trip, could benefit if the leaders overextend slightly, though both are racing from naturally further back than ideal given field congestion at the rear; this scenario requires an untypically strong gallop for a lone front-runner race.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos — Traffic Issues Decide
scenarios.trigger: If a congested midfield creates significant interference in the straight, producing an unpredictable finish.
scenarios.body: With multiple hold-up types forced into a tighter midfield than their natural role, traffic problems in the straight could disrupt the form horses and hand the race to one who finds clear daylight at the right moment; Ashen, with a versatile enough profile and confidence from a recent win, would be best placed to exploit any opening.

watchPoints.text: Watch whether Blakefell jumps cleanly and immediately asserts — if Tom Eaves cannot slot to the front uncontested in the first furlong, the entire pace dynamic shifts and the race opens up considerably.

The Gay Blade has won three of his last four over 7f on Good including this course — if Andrew Mullen positions him immediately behind Blakefell and the gallop is steady, he becomes the primary danger without needing anything to go wrong elsewhere.

Ashen carries the joint top weight of 135lbs alongside Blakefell and Eve's Boy — watch how Lauren Young (5lb claimer) deploys him early, as his recent course form and winning ability make him a credible factor if he can secure a handy enough position.

Multiple hold-up horses including Abduction, Slack Bob and Native Honey will be competing for the same late run — monitor how congested the straight becomes, as traffic interference in the final 2f is a genuine risk given the field composition.

Qazaq ran just three days ago — watch for any signs of flatness in the paddock or early in the race, as horses on very quick turnarounds at this level can lack the sharpness to compete if the pace is even remotely testing.

races.name: Try Racing TV For Free Now Handicap

runners_data.name: Hunterian
runners_data.note: Won last time out over 8f on soft, handles good going competently, and Sean Bowen's booking for Charlie Johnston is notable; races from hold-up but has placed form on good, and with only 1W from 7 sim-going runs he needs everything to fall right tactically.

runners_data.name: Carmel Valley
runners_data.note: Joanna Mason takes the mount for trainer Katie Scott but consistent form figures of 7s across recent good-ground outings offer little hope; unclassified style and no wins or places on similar going in four attempts makes this a tough ask at OR 62.

runners_data.name: Hey Havana
runners_data.note: Clifford Lee partners a horse with solid placed form on good ground — six runs on similar going yielding two places — and a prominent racing style that maps perfectly to a Penelope's Sister-led race; the drop back to 1m from 7f trips is the one query but recent 2nds on good suggest she handles it.

runners_data.name: Flying Moonlight
runners_data.note: Sandy Thomson's filly has shown improvement with a recent 3rd on soft but her natural instinct is to come from deep; she finds herself mapped to midfield in a race with too many closers, meaning she is unlikely to switch off or get the late run she needs — seven from seven blanks on good going compounds the concern.

runners_data.name: Lightning Galaxy
runners_data.note: Michael Dods' four-year-old has the tongue-tie applied and carries top weight at 136lbs; a genuine closer by preference, she is among the hold-up types displaced into a midfield berth, and eight from eleven unplaced runs on good going tells a blunt story — Connor Beasley will need significant luck in running.

runners_data.name: Lovette
runners_data.note: Iain Jardine has a 4/34 14-day strike rate and the tp headgear is retained, but Lovette's true closing style means she is pushed into the midfield pack in a race with surplus rear-guard runners; won once on good going from eleven starts and placed once — needs a pace collapse that this race shape is unlikely to provide.

runners_data.name: Concert Boy
runners_data.note: Greg Fairley rides for trainer Katie Scott, who has sent out zero winners from 19 runners in the 14-day window — a sobering number; a prominent-style six-year-old who has been placed as recently as 2nd at 7f on standard, but only one placing from 15 similar-going runs is hard to ignore at OR 55.

runners_data.name: Filly Eilish
runners_data.note: Tom Eaves partners Ivan Furtado's filly who has an unclassified style and is 31 days fresh; dropping back from 10f trips is the key question, and with only one similar-going run showing a placing, the form on good ground is thinner than her OR 64 might suggest.

runners_data.name: Starliner
runners_data.note: The five-year-old with headgear (p) has won on good over 8f and placed twice more in five such runs — the best strike rate of any closer in the field — and Kaiya Fraser takes the ride for Linda Perratt; 31 days off, top weight at 142lbs, and a natural hold-up style that is at least genuine rather than redistributed, making him the closest thing to a credible late-race threat.

runners_data.name: Penelope's Sister
runners_data.note: Paul Mulrennan's mount for Jim Goldie (6/36 in 14 days) is the confirmed pace-setter, though her five recent runs have produced placings at OR 61 on soft and good, and the style-fit flag acknowledges she is likely to be exposed as the race develops; the key asset is uncontested lead access, not raw form quality.

runners_data.name: Ey Up He's A Star
runners_data.note: Tony Coyle & Kaine Wood's four-year-old carries the p headgear and has three recent placings on good going — the most of any hold-up runner here; David Nolan, an experienced handler of pace scenarios, gives this horse a tactical edge, and 22 days since last run is not a concern given recent consistency.

races.paceDynamic: Penelope's Sister is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine rival likely to press her hard from the off, she should be able to dictate a steady-to-moderate gallop over this flat Ayr mile on good ground. Hey Havana and Concert Boy are the principal prominent-style horses likely to track her through the early stages, creating a race that unfolds at a controlled tempo rather than a true searching test of stamina. The field holds more hold-up types than can realistically be accommodated at the rear — Lovette, Lightning Galaxy, and Flying Moonlight are all natural closers who will be squeezed into a midfield cluster rather than their preferred position, meaning their finishing kicks may be partially neutralised. A race run at a sustainable clip from the front with limited genuine pace pressure overwhelmingly favours horses racing prominently or just off the leader, as the sprint for home will reward those who save ground and avoid traffic rather than those closing from deep.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Front Runner Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Penelope's Sister is allowed to bowl along unchallenged and the pace remains steady throughout.
scenarios.body: She sets the fractions she wants over the flat mile, the field strings out behind her, and those sitting just off her heels travelling comfortably are perfectly placed entering the final two furlongs; Hey Havana and Hunterian, with their ability to race handily, are ideally positioned to pounce as the leader inevitably ties.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Horses Quicken
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is honest enough that the front-runner is headed at the two-furlong pole and a prominent or handy tracker quickens past.
scenarios.body: Hey Havana's good-ground placed form and willingness to race in touch makes him the natural beneficiary as the race ignites in the straight; Hunterian, who won last time on soft and handles good, can produce a strong late challenge from just off the pace.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is surprisingly strong and the field comes back to the closers in the final furlong, giving the rear-guard a genuine run at them.
scenarios.body: Starliner has solid good-ground credentials at this trip and, if the race develops a true-enough gallop, can deliver a sustained late charge; Ey Up He's A Star has shown placed form on good going and would also benefit, though both are relying on a pace scenario that the redistribution of hold-up types makes less likely.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaotic Contested Pace
scenarios.trigger: If Concert Boy or Hey Havana challenges Penelope's Sister aggressively early, creating a genuinely hot gallop that blows the race wide open.
scenarios.body: A fierce early duel would see the front and prominent horses fade in the closing stages, handing momentum to any horse with a clean passage; Hunterian, with his most recent win and versatile profile, and Filly Eilish, stepping back in trip, would be best placed to capitalise on a messy, collapsed-pace finale.

watchPoints.text: Penelope's Sister (front runner) — watch whether she is allowed a soft lead or whether Hey Havana or Concert Boy push forward to challenge her early; if she bowls clear unchallenged, the race is effectively decided within the first two furlongs tactically.

Starliner — the only hold-up horse with a genuine good-ground winning profile at this trip; if she gets a clean passage from the rear into the straight she is the principal threat to the prominent handlers, but traffic in a bunched midfield group could end her chance before the home turn.

Lightning Galaxy, Lovette, and Flying Moonlight — all three genuine closers compressed into the midfield; watch for early crowding between the 6f-4f marks where their natural inclination to drop back meets the artificial positioning, creating a potential pocket of trouble.

Hunterian — Sean Bowen's booking for Charlie Johnston from a hold-up base with recent winning form is the standout jockey-trainer angle; watch how early Bowen sends him to race prominently given the likely slow pace, as switching tactics could make him the most versatile runner in the field.

Concert Boy — a prominent-style runner for a trainer with zero wins from 19 recent runners; if he breaks sharply and pressures Penelope's Sister from the off, the entire pace dynamic shifts, so his early position in the first furlong is worth monitoring closely.

races.name: Ladbrokes Get More With Racing Bet Builder Ayr Silver Cup Trial Handicap

runners_data.name: Territorial Knight
runners_data.note: The confirmed front runner of the race; four wins from 14 starts on similar going and fresh off a 65-day break, Kevin Ryan horses often return well; the STYLE_FIT flag means if pushed wide or harried, his advantage diminishes significantly.

runners_data.name: Gweedore
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old hold-up type for Katie Scott, trainer in modest 14-day form (1/12); all recent runs over 7f and limited wins on Good ground, the drop to 6f on a flat course looks the main concern.

runners_data.name: Woven
runners_data.note: Veteran hold-up horse at ten years old with headgear noted; Connor Beasley keeps him in the front half of results at times and his last run was a close second over this trip on Good — retains ability but consistency is the issue.

runners_data.name: Jordan Electrics
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer with a flagged tendency to fade in the finish, a concern in what may be a slowly-run 6f; Jim Goldie sends him out on a short 19-day turnaround and recent form (026954) does not inspire confidence.

runners_data.name: Rousing Encore
runners_data.note: Prominent-style runner for Ruth Carr, whose 14-day strike rate is modest (1/27); all five recent runs over this 6f trip on Good ground returned two fifths and a fourth as best — honest but lacks a killer finish in a compressed field.

runners_data.name: Misunderstood
runners_data.note: David O'Meara's hold-up horse returned 31 days ago; recent form includes a fifth at 6f on Good but the yard's 14-day record (8/52) is workmanlike rather than flying — the step back to 6f from longer trips in recent starts is a mild positive.

runners_data.name: Lord Bertie
runners_data.note: Stablemate of Misunderstood, also from the O'Meara yard with headgear noted; the 5/15 similar-going record and 0 wins at 6f on Good are telling, and a run of 11th, 12th, 6th and 15th in the last four outings suggests he is below his best currently.

runners_data.name: Parisiac
runners_data.note: Prominent racer boasting genuine course-and-distance form including a recent win at 5f on Good; Iain Jardine's yard has been firing (7/31 in 14 days) and the 7lb claimer Cara Tuke keeps the weight down — the most progressive profile in the prominent group.

runners_data.name: Manila Scouse
runners_data.note: A true hold-up performer by nature but the overcrowded rear means he will be forced forward into midfield, away from his best position; Tim Easterby's stable is busy (7/92) and the horse has strong similar-going form (12/15), but the positional compromise is real.

runners_data.name: Prince Of Pillo
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse who will find himself racing in midfield against his instincts due to the volume of closers; poor recent form (02-968) and limited form on this going (3/15) make him a difficult proposition regardless of position.

runners_data.name: Dakota Gold
runners_data.note: A twelve-year-old who races off the pace by preference — his true hold-up role is compromised by redistribution into midfield; last run was a finishing twentieth on Good ground over 6f, suggesting age may be catching up despite historic course form.

runners_data.name: Here Forever
runners_data.note: Three-year-old for David & Nicola Barron with a win at 6f on Good in the book (1/6f/GOO) and a perfect 5/5 similar-going record; the trainer's 14-day record is bare (0/8) and the horse races from the back naturally, which the pace map cannot fully accommodate.

runners_data.name: The Caltonian
runners_data.note: Hold-up type whose recent form is built on Standard going (AW) rather than turf — only 2 from 15 on similar turf going; Linda Perratt's yard is quiet (0/9 in 14 days) and the 7-year-old steps back onto turf after a short 9-day turnaround.

runners_data.name: Cotai Lights
runners_data.note: Prominent-style three-year-old for Adrian Paul Keatley returning after a 50-day break; best form on Good going over 6-7f (two thirds) but yet to win, and the layoff adds uncertainty over readiness on the day.

runners_data.name: Dandy Magic
runners_data.note: Four-year-old returning 16 days after a run on Standard ground; Jim Goldie's runner holds a hold-up profile but will be mapped into midfield — recent form is moderate (52300) and the single similar-going run (1/15) underlines the ground concern.

runners_data.name: Tip Foster
runners_data.note: Lightly raced three-year-old (only two career runs) with a win at 7f on Good and a placed run at 6f on Soft — the inexperience flag is real in an 18-runner handicap sprint; running style is unknown, which adds further tactical uncertainty.

runners_data.name: Daizen
runners_data.note: Rebecca Menzies' three-year-old winner at 6f on Good (1/6f/GOO) and Soft; trainer has a quiet 14-day spell (0/23) and the horse is a hold-up type displaced into midfield — the positional compromise is the main obstacle rather than lack of ability.

runners_data.name: Kelpie Grey
runners_data.note: Lowest-rated runner in the field (OR=66) and a true hold-up performer shuffled into midfield; Jim Goldie's record over 14 days is solid (7/44) but the horse's form at 6f on Good is limited (0 wins, 3 places in 15 runs) and the weight of evidence suggests a place at best.

races.paceDynamic: Territorial Knight is the lone confirmed front runner in this 18-runner 6f handicap and, with no genuine pace rival to press him, he should be able to dictate from the gates at a controlled, sustainable gallop on Good ground at Ayr. Rousing Encore, Parisiac and Cotai Lights will try to press close behind, creating a compact early order, but none of these is a true front runner and they are unlikely to generate a searching pace that burns Territorial Knight off. The resulting shape is a steadily-run race that sets up for horses racing prominently or just off the pace, giving them a clean run into the straight with plenty left in the tank — closers and true hold-up types will find the gap between them and the leaders too large to bridge in six furlongs without a strong gallop to chase. This field holds significantly more hold-up horses than the pace map can accommodate at the rear; Manila Scouse, Here Forever, Prince Of Pillo, Dakota Gold, Daizen, Kelpie Grey, Dandy Magic and The Caltonian are genuine hold-up types who will be forced to race closer than ideal, with Territorial Knight and Parisiac most likely to actually secure their natural front or prominent positions. The race shape strongly favours a prominent racing profile — horses that can travel close to the compressed early pace, avoid traffic and kick once the race quickens in the final two furlongs.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Territorial Knight Front Leads
scenarios.trigger: If Territorial Knight bowls along unchallenged and the pace stays controlled throughout the six furlongs.
scenarios.body: Territorial Knight dictates a sustainable pace from stall to home straight, and with no rival able or willing to put him under serious pressure, he conserves energy and quickens away in the final furlong; prominent types behind him enjoy a smooth trip in a small, fast-moving group.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Collide Late
scenarios.trigger: If Parisiac or Rousing Encore press Territorial Knight hard early, fractionally lifting the tempo and weakening the front runner.
scenarios.body: A slightly stronger pace than scenario A unfolds, bringing the mid-division prominent horses into the finish on the heels of a tiring leader; horses with a high Racing Post Rating who can travel in second or third without fighting for position are best placed.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Strike From Deep
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is stronger than expected due to multiple prominent types crowding forward and the leaders tie up inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: The moderate early gallop becomes a sprint up the straight but the redistribution of true hold-up horses into midfield means several of them are already closer than usual, and the best of them land running at the right moment; this scenario is discounted because the supposed closers are not true hold-up types.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front Runner Fades Badly
scenarios.trigger: If Territorial Knight is harried wide or into too fast an early pace by over-eager rivals and the field strings out.
scenarios.body: A contested early pace would drain Territorial Knight and the race develops into a test of stamina for a flat 6f sprint, opening the door for horses with strong late sections and proven Good-ground form; this is the least likely shape given the clear shortage of genuine pace rivals willing to take on the leader.

watchPoints.text: Territorial Knight's draw and early behaviour from the gates are critical — if he is slow away or harried by Parisiac or Rousing Encore in the first furlong, the controlled pace the race shape depends on collapses immediately.

Parisiac's combination of recent winning form, a busy in-form trainer (Iain Jardine 7/31) and a prominent position that suits the pace map makes him the most likely beneficiary if Territorial Knight does not dominate early.

The cluster of redistributed hold-up horses — Manila Scouse, Here Forever, Daizen, Dandy Magic and Kelpie Grey — will create significant traffic in the first half of the field; watch for trouble in running when the straight is reached and the pace quickens.

Here Forever's unbeaten 5/5 similar-going record on Good turf is the standout conditional statistic in the field and warrants monitoring if she secures a cleaner run than the redistribution scenario suggests she will.

Tip Foster's unknown running style and extreme inexperience (two career runs) in a field of 18 is a live source of disruption — if she breaks prominently she could compromise the positional plans of Rousing Encore or Cotai Lights directly behind Territorial Knight.

races.name: 25% Off Lunch At Western House Hotel Handicap

runners_data.name: Henery Hawk
runners_data.note: The only confirmed front-runner here and likely to lead from flag to finish; trainer Linda Perratt has a poor 14-day strike rate (0/8) and the horse has been running over 5f on standard recently, making the step up to 6f on good ground a mild query, but the uncontested lead is a significant tactical asset.

runners_data.name: Joshuas Dream
runners_data.note: A 247-day absence is a serious fitness concern for this 2-year-old making just its second start on turf; Jim Goldie sends it out fresh but that layoff combined with modest similar-going form (0W1P from 6 runs) makes this very much a watch-and-learn run.

runners_data.name: Keep The Gold
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer fitted with a hood; Connor Beasley is a reliable booking and the horse has placed consistently on good ground (three placings from nine similar-going runs), suggesting it handles conditions but may need a stronger gallop than this race is likely to produce.

runners_data.name: April Diamond
runners_data.note: Recent form shows a good second over 6f on good ground, making conditions right; Andrew Mullen takes the ride and the horse is a genuine hold-up type, though the overcrowded rear means it is likely to have to race closer to the pace than ideal, partially compromising its natural finishing style.

runners_data.name: White Ladder
runners_data.note: Sean D Bowen is a significant jockey booking from the jumping sphere and worth noting; the mare has consistent placed form at 6-7f on good ground (five placings from eight similar-going runs) and races from hold-up, but a steady pace on this flat track may blunt her finishing effort.

runners_data.name: Maynora
runners_data.note: Fitted with a hood and had a run 11 days ago keeping it fresh; Clifford Lee rides for Craig Lidster who has a quiet 14-day record (0/16), and the horse's one win came on soft ground — the step back to good may slightly reduce its chance of finding extra late.

runners_data.name: Royal Duke
runners_data.note: The trainer R Mike Smith has a positive 14-day record (2/21) and this horse has two wins and four places from 15 similar-going runs, suggesting it genuinely handles these conditions; a true hold-up type that will be forced to race further forward than ideal given the crowded rear, which partially negates its style strengths.

runners_data.name: So Grateful
runners_data.note: An 8-year-old with modest recent form (positions 10, 9, 7, 9, 13 in last five) and a Billy Garritty booking; has one win from 15 good-ground runs and its natural hold-up style is compromised by the field's overcrowded back end — the form and age profile make this hard to recommend.

runners_data.name: Saxon Grace
runners_data.note: Fitted with a hood for this meeting (T14: 1/4 for trainer Daragh Bourke); has posted consistent midfield finishes (4th, 4th, 6th) on good ground and at 6f, though as a genuine hold-up horse pushed into the midfield map, a sedate pace here is a significant obstacle to finishing strongly.

runners_data.name: Ellie's de Vega
runners_data.note: An admirably consistent horse with four thirds from five runs on good ground and a genuine prominent racing style; Ryan Sexton's booking is straightforward and the horse is one of only three natural front-rank types in the field, giving it an excellent positional advantage if it can slot in just behind Henery Hawk.

runners_data.name: Newyorkstateofmind
runners_data.note: A 9-year-old fitted with blinkers and returning 10 days after its last run; James Sullivan rides for Ruth Carr who has a quiet 14-day record (0/30), and the horse's true hold-up profile means it will be running from further back than the race shape ideally serves, with modest recent finishing positions confirming limited current form.

runners_data.name: Baby Rover
runners_data.note: Joanna Mason rides for Katie Scott (1/11 in 14 days) and the horse ran a solid second over 6f on good ground in its best recent effort; one of only three prominent-style runners, it is well positioned to sit in behind Henery Hawk and have every chance if the gallop is as steady as expected.

runners_data.name: Saxon Gem
runners_data.note: The Jim Goldie yard has been active (6/37 in 14 days) but this 3-year-old has finished no better than 4th in five runs on good ground; Lauren Young claims 5lbs and the horse's natural hold-up style, combined with its uninspiring recent form record at 6f on good, makes it one of the harder cases to make in this field.

races.paceDynamic: Henery Hawk is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine rival to push the pace, should stride into an uncontested lead from the gates and control the tempo throughout this 6f handicap on good ground at Ayr. Ellie's de Vega and Baby Rover are the only other prominent-style runners but neither has the natural lead-seeking profile to seriously challenge Henery Hawk for the front, meaning the pace is unlikely to be truly hot — a sustainable, measured gallop is the most probable shape. This controlled tempo over six furlongs on a flat, fair track favours horses who can race prominently or in the first half of the field and sustain their effort through the final two furlongs, rather than those relying on a strong pace to close into. The field holds significantly more hold-up types than the track can accommodate at the rear — April Diamond, Saxon Grace, Royal Duke, So Grateful, Saxon Gem, and Newyorkstateofmind are all true hold-up horses redistributed into midfield because genuine back-of-the-field positions are oversupplied; of these, April Diamond and Saxon Grace, with their better recent form, are most likely to actually secure a forward midfield position in running. The dominant tactical verdict is clear: prominent runners who can slot in close to Henery Hawk's sustainable lead hold the decisive positional advantage in this race shape.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hawk Controls, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Henery Hawk leads at a comfortable gallop and no rival applies early pressure, allowing the race to be run at a steady-to-moderate tempo throughout.
scenarios.body: Henery Hawk dictates from the front without being challenged, and horses racing in the prominent group immediately behind are perfectly placed to kick entering the final furlong; with closers unable to generate the momentum a fast pace would give them, the race is won from the first three positions.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Front Pair Clear
scenarios.trigger: If Henery Hawk and one of the prominent runners (Ellie's de Vega or Baby Rover) draw well clear of a strung-out field in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: A modest early gallop leaves the hold-up horses with too much ground to make up in the closing stages, and the prominent pair find themselves racing in clear air; the first two home are drawn from the lead/prominent group, with the midfield runners unable to close the gap in time.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Stronger Pace, Closers Land
scenarios.trigger: If early pressure builds — either Ellie's de Vega or Baby Rover pushes Henery Hawk into a faster gallop than he would naturally set — and the front runners tire.
scenarios.body: A genuinely competitive early pace stretches the field and opens the door for the better-quality hold-up horses to finish strongly in the final furlong; April Diamond, who has shown a strong finishing effort on good ground (2nd/6f/Good), and White Ladder, who is consistent at this trip, are best placed to benefit.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos, Big-Field Scramble
scenarios.trigger: If there is significant positional jostling early, with multiple horses attempting to get prominent, causing uneven fractions and a bunched finish.
scenarios.body: Disrupted early running breaks the anticipated pattern, and a horse coming from slightly off the pace finds a clean run through to grab the spoils late; with the redistribution of so many hold-up types into the midfield, the benefit is marginal and this scenario remains unlikely given the clear pace hierarchy.

watchPoints.text: Henery Hawk sets the entire tempo of this race — watch the opening two furlongs to see whether Ellie's de Vega or Baby Rover force the front-runner into a faster gallop than anticipated, which would fundamentally change which profiles benefit.

April Diamond and Royal Duke are genuine hold-up horses mapped forward due to field overcrowding — if the draw or early running allows them to drop back to their natural position, they lose their forced positional benefit, but if pinned forward too early they may tire.

White Ladder's jockey Sean D Bowen is primarily a jump jockey — monitor his positioning in the early stages, as any unfamiliarity with flat tactics at Ayr over 6f could leave the horse wide or poorly placed entering the closing stages.

Joshuas Dream returns from a 247-day absence and is only a 2-year-old; watch how freely it travels early, as any signs of greenness or fitness shortage will confirm this is a racecourse educational run rather than a genuine winning attempt.

The hood wearers Maynora and Saxon Grace (and Royal Duke's reapplication of good-ground form) are worth watching in the pre-race paddock and early canter — headgear can sharpen or unsettle, and any signs of agitation could affect their ability to race prominently as the field overcrowding demands.

races.name: Dream Weddings At Western House Hotel Handicap

runners_data.name: Elemental Eye
runners_data.note: Races from well off the pace for Iain Jardine, holds a win at this sort of trip on Standard and form figures suggest she needs things to go wrong for others; Andrew Mullen takes the ride and 9 days since last run is fine, but the blinkered mare has struggled to convert placed efforts into wins on Good recently.

runners_data.name: Idyllic
runners_data.note: Paula Muir takes the 3lb claim for Wilf Storey, who has a modest 14-day strike rate, and 1 day since last run is an eyecatcher that merits caution — horses turned around this quickly at this level can be fresh or fatigued; a natural hold-up type whose best form is on softer ground than today.

runners_data.name: Annandale
runners_data.note: Jim Goldie's eight-year-old has genuine course-and-distance ability with two wins in recent similar-going history, and Paul Mulrennan is a strong booking; his true preference is to be produced late but with the field compacted he will need to settle for a midfield berth rather than the rear he'd ideally want.

runners_data.name: Is She Now
runners_data.note: Back-to-back wins are solid credentials and David Nolan is an experienced pilot, but her most recent venture over this sort of distance produced an 18th — the form needs careful filtering; she's a natural hold-up type who will be shuffled into midfield by the weight of similar runners, and her Good-going record of seven runs returning just one win and one placing is unimpressive.

runners_data.name: Galahad Threepwood
runners_data.note: The nine-year-old for Ewan Whillans has form in staying races up to 21f, so stamina is not the concern; Greg Fairley rides and the horse is a genuine hold-up operator who will find himself racing more prominently than he'd like, a positional compromise that has historically blunted his effectiveness.

runners_data.name: Aighear
runners_data.note: Jim Goldie saddles this eight-year-old who shows a string of placed efforts — three third-place finishes in the last five starts — and the 15-16f range suits; Lauren Young's 5lb claim softens the weight, and though she wants to come from deep, the compressed field means she'll be mid-pack, which may actually suit if the pace is genuine.

runners_data.name: Ebony Maw
runners_data.note: Connor Beasley partners the tongue-tied, blinker-wearing nine-year-old for Whillans, and the headgear combination suggests the horse needs plenty of help to concentrate; his Good-going record (one placed from four in similar conditions) is modest and he'll be pushed wider than ideal given the number of hold-up rivals.

runners_data.name: La Tosca
runners_data.note: The three-year-old for Charlie Johnston is the class angle — Johnston is in excellent 14-day form (9/67) and Sean Bowen is a high-quality jockey parachuted in; consistent placed form including five seconds in recent starts suggests a reliable galloper who lacks a finishing kick, so the uncontested pace suits a horse happy to track and grind rather than sprint.

runners_data.name: This Rib
runners_data.note: The sole front-runner by style in this field, David Loughnane's three-year-old is tagged with a tongue-tie and will bowl along from the gates for Joanna Mason; her form over 7-8f is not obviously suited to 1m5f and zero wins from five runs on going better than Soft raises stamina questions, but the total lack of any pace rival gives her every chance to steal this with a measured front-running display.

races.paceDynamic: This Rib is the sole confirmed front-runner in a nine-runner field over 1m5f at Ayr on Good ground, and with no genuine rival willing to dispute the lead, she is set to bowl along at a sustainable, uncontested gallop from the outset. The rest of the field — Elemental Eye, Idyllic, Annandale, Is She Now, Galahad Threepwood, Aighear, Ebony Maw and La Tosca — are all natural hold-up or come-from-behind types, meaning This Rib faces zero pressure through the early and middle stages. The field holds considerably more hold-up horses than the race shape can organically accommodate at the rear — Annandale, Is She Now, Galahad Threepwood and Aighear are the most likely to be pushed forward into a midfield position rather than settling in their preferred ground, which compresses the field and creates a train rather than a true test of stamina. An uncontested pace on Good turf over this distance strongly favours hold-up closers who can produce a sustained run from the home turn, making runners who relish a true test of stamina from the back the primary beneficiaries — provided the pace This Rib sets is honest enough to stop her from stealing it unchallenged.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: This Rib Steals It
scenarios.trigger: If This Rib is allowed to dictate a comfortable, uncontested pace and the hold-up field fails to organise a meaningful pursuit until too late.
scenarios.body: This Rib strolls into a commanding lead through the back straight, the compressed hold-up field wastes ground tracking each other, and by the time closers wind up their challenge the gap is too great to bridge.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Closers Overhaul
scenarios.trigger: If the hold-up runners time their runs well from the home turn and the pace proves just honest enough to stop This Rib from conserving too much energy.
scenarios.body: Annandale and Is She Now, both capable on Good ground at this sort of trip, get competitive mid-race positions and produce sustained finishes to collar a fading leader in the closing stages.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Grinders Land
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely moderate and the race degenerates into a sprint from the home bend, favouring horses who can quicken from a handy position.
scenarios.body: La Tosca, consistent and placed repeatedly at this sort of level, and Aighear from a tracking position benefit most from a falsely-run race that rewards a turn of foot rather than stamina.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Field Falls Apart
scenarios.trigger: If a ragged pace creates a chaotic home straight with several horses interfering with each other as the compressed hold-up group all make moves simultaneously.
scenarios.body: Elemental Eye or Idyllic, running wide of trouble from deeper in the field, pick up the pieces as the main contenders block each other out, turning a messy race into an opportunity for a previously out-of-form runner.

watchPoints.text: Watch whether This Rib is allowed a completely uncontested lead through the first mile — if Joanna Mason finds no rival willing to go with her, the margin she builds could prove insurmountable regardless of how well the closers travel.

Annandale and Is She Now are both genuine hold-up types forced into midfield positions; if they spend energy establishing early position rather than relaxing, their finishing kicks will be blunted — monitor how they settle in the first half-mile.

La Tosca's consistent placed record (0W5P in recent form) makes her a reliable frame candidate but questions whether she can add a win — Sean Bowen's quality could make the difference, but watch whether she gets a clear run as the field concertinas in the home straight.

Idyllic ran just 1 day ago — a quick turnaround for Wilf Storey's yard, which has a limited 14-day record; monitor market moves and paddock condition as a horse in anything less than peak physical shape may find this 1m5f on Good ground unforgiving.

Aighear's three recent third-place finishes on Soft suggest she's consistent but may find Good ground faster than ideal — if the going rides on the lively side of Good after a day of racing, her profile becomes slightly less compelling.
